packages.title: «Como el teléfono» follows a phone-language change while the app runs
brief: UX-1653 (S2), regression R2D-1 from P215 (verify-b5-r2-D). What the last round did: P215 (UX-1649, verified fixed) made `AppLanguageBridge.phoneLocales` (`App/lib/services/app_language.dart:23-31`) the source of "the phone's languages" for the app's `locale:` and `RegionalMaterialDelegate` (`App/lib/main.dart:433-451`), the recognizer (`native_speech.dart:198-200`), the Idioma sheet's subtitle (`language_selector.dart:84-90`) and background reminders (`App/lib/services/reminder_copy.dart:12-17`, saved row before `PlatformDispatcher`). Its brief said not to re-apply on `didChangeLocales`, for fear of a loop. Why it fails: only `apply` sets `phoneLocales`, and it runs only at start (`main.dart:101`) and when Idioma changes (`language_selector.dart:65`). The activity declares `locale` in `configChanges` (`App/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:28`), so a phone-language change while the process is alive arrives only as `didChangeLocales` (`main.dart:135-139`). With Idioma «Como el teléfono» (the default) the app then keeps the stale list and stays in the old language until the process dies; `TaskReminders.refreshLanguage()` (`main.dart:138`), whose job is exactly this case, rewrites the reminders in the old language; and background reminders read the stale saved row ahead of `PlatformDispatcher`. Before P215 all of these followed the phone at once. The loop fear doesn't hold: `AppLanguageBridge.kt:40` sets `applicationLocales` only when they differ, so the one change a re-apply can cause (Idioma English with a new phone region, `en-ES` to `en-FR`) comes back once, finds them equal and stops.

(a) `App/lib/main.dart:135-139`, `didChangeLocales`: keep `if (mounted) setState(() {});` and replace `unawaited(TaskReminders.refreshLanguage());` with `unawaited(AppLanguageBridge.apply(ref.read(regionalProvider).language).then((_) => TaskReminders.refreshLanguage()));`. The bridge answers with the phone's fresh tags, sets `phoneLocales` (which notifies `AppLanguageBridge.phone`, so `_phoneLocalesChanged` rebuilds `MaterialApp` with the new `locale:` and week start) and saves the row, and only then are the reminders rewritten. `apply` never throws (it catches) and returns at once off Android, so the reminder refresh still runs there exactly as today. Add a one-line comment: re-asking can't loop because the bridge sets the per-app language only when it differs. If P215 left a comment anywhere saying the language must not be re-applied on a locale change, correct it.

(b) `App/lib/services/reminder_copy.dart:12-17`, `_phoneLocales`: pass in the `RegionalPreferences` both callers already read (`readReminderStrings` `:32`, `readReminderCopy` `:41`), as `_phoneLocales(TaskDatabase database, RegionalPreferences preferences)`. Order: `AppLanguageBridge.phoneLocales`; then, when `preferences.language == AppLanguages.system` (`App/lib/l10n/app_languages.dart:6`), `PlatformDispatcher.instance.locales`; then `AppLanguageBridge.readSavedPhoneLocales(database)`; then `PlatformDispatcher.instance.locales`. Reason, for the doc comment: with «Como el teléfono» no per-app language is set, so Flutter's locales are the phone's and live, also in a background isolate; the saved copy is needed only when Idioma names a language, because Flutter then reports the app's. Keep the `deviceLocales` parameter of both functions exactly as it is; tests pass it.

Don't touch: `AppLanguageBridge.kt`; `app_language.dart` (`apply`, the saved row, `readSavedPhoneLocales`, `phoneOr` stay as P215 left them); `main()`'s first-frame seeding (`main.dart:55-58`); `build` (`:433-451`) and `localeListResolutionCallback`; `language_selector.dart` and `native_speech.dart` (they follow `phoneLocales` once (a) refreshes it); P216's and P217's changes. Changing Idioma now also makes one extra `apply` through the locale change it raises; that is expected and returns the same answer. No copy, ARB, native or manifest changes, so neither gen-l10n nor an APK build is needed.

Tests: keep the whole suite passing. P215's implementer reported that `App/test/capture_landing_test.dart` UX-1628 ('resuming 31 minutes later') failed near midnight with and without P215's change (it reads `DateTime.now()`); if it fails, check whether it also fails without this package's change and say so in your notes rather than editing it.
acceptance: Widget test, Android target, Idioma «Como el teléfono», Flutter's locales `es-ES`, the `taskflow/app-language` channel answering `['es-ES']`: the app is in Spanish. Then the channel answers `['ca-ES']` and the test sets Flutter's locales to `ca-ES` (a `didChangeLocales`): after pumping, `Localizations.localeOf(context).languageCode` is `ca` and a visible app string (for example the Calendar tab label from `AppLocalizations` ca) is Catalan, without restarting the app.

Same test: the locale change makes exactly one more `apply` call on the channel, with `languages: []`; afterwards `AppLanguageBridge.phoneLocales` is `[ca-ES]` and the saved `phone-locales` row reads `['ca-ES']`.
Same test: the reminder refresh runs after the bridge answered: `readReminderStrings(database)` (no `deviceLocales`) called right after the pump returns Catalan strings.

Unit: Idioma «Como el teléfono», the `phone-locales` row saved as `['es-ES']`, `phoneLocales` null (a background isolate), `PlatformDispatcher` locales `ca-ES`: `readReminderStrings(database)` is Catalan and `readReminderCopy(database, system24Hour: true)` resolves its language to `ca`.

Unit: Idioma English, week start «Como el teléfono», the row saved as `['es-ES']`, `phoneLocales` null, `PlatformDispatcher` locales `en-ES`: `readReminderCopy` still takes the phone's `es-ES` as its device locale (UX-1649's acceptance tests pass unchanged).
Off Android: a `didChangeLocales` makes no channel call and still refreshes the reminders' language; every existing regional, language and reminder test passes unchanged.
deviceChecks: Emulator lane, Android 13+, Idioma «Como el teléfono», app open in Spanish: send it to the background, switch the phone's language to Català in Android settings, return: TaskFlow is in Catalan without being restarted. Record whether Android kept the process alive (if it didn't, the cold start already covers this case on that device).
Emulator lane: same setup, app swiped away after the change, a reminder fires: its text is Catalan.

Emulator lane: Idioma English, phone Spanish (Spain); switch the phone's region to United States: the app stays English, the week strip follows the phone's new first day, and the screen settles at once (no repeated flashing; logcat shows no repeated configuration changes).
